A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViT3 study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and supplementary Sections 7–9 are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TTT design ablations, classification, detection, segmentation and generation experiments, and throughput/memory measurements in Tables 1–10 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original ablation, downstream-task and efficiency results in Tables 1–10 and Figures 3–4.

M1.justification: Sections 5 and 9 retain the same ViT3 architecture: one full-batch inner update with learning rate 1.0 and dot-product loss, combining simplified gated linear units with depthwise convolution. No algorithm or architecture change is documented.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet-1K for classification and generation, COCO for detection/instance segmentation, and ADE20K for semantic segmentation. The resolution-based efficiency scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 5 and 7–10, including the convolutional, Transformer, Mamba, linear-attention and DiT comparisons. The newly cited circulant-attention paper is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Reported evaluation settings remain unchanged. Section 4 newly specifies DeiT-S and ImageNet-1K with 300 training epochs for the existing design study; this clarifies previously underspecified settings without documenting a protocol revision.

E4.justification: The same loss, batch-size, inner-epoch, learning-rate, model-width/depth, convolution, residual-connection and initialization analyses remain in Tables 1–4 and 6 and Figure 3. The efficiency analysis in Figure 4 is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point results and training/efficiency curves without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–10 and the plotted findings in Figures 3–4 are retained. For example, ViT3-S remains at 81.6% top-1 accuracy in Table 7, and DiT3-B/2 retains FID 39.31 in Table 10.

T1.justification: The attention/TTT definitions, mixed-derivative argument, learning-rate rescaling derivation and supplementary loss derivatives remain unchanged in Equations 1–17.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: six practical TTT design insights, a pure linear-complexity ViT3 architecture, and competitive performance across the evaluated vision tasks.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning causal mini-batch bias, deep-inner-model optimization difficulties and convolutional global/local integration are retained. Section 7 preserves the same limitations concerning unexplored optimizers, inner data augmentation and Transformer inner models.

D1.justification: Section 4 changes the generic backbone description from DeiT to DeiT-S and explicitly identifies ImageNet-1K and 300 epochs for the design study. This improves documentation of existing experiments. Architecture Tables 11–13 and the actual code-link destination are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Han et al., Vision Transformers Are Circulant Attention Learners, as reference 24 in v2. Research positioning otherwise remains unchanged; publication updates for Titans and Test-Time Training Done Right refer to already cited works.

P1.justification: Limited edits clarify Section 4, replace the abstract's 'this URL' wording with the repository address, and update funding and bibliographic metadata. The narrative, section order and supplementary explanations remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is reduced in size, vertical spacing becomes more compact, text flows across different column/page boundaries, and printed page numbers are removed. All four figures and thirteen tables remain, with unchanged table structures and plotted content.

improvement.justification: Section 4 now explicitly identifies the DeiT-S backbone and ImageNet-1K/300-epoch setup for the existing ablations, reducing ambiguity about their configuration. This provides a limited reproducibility improvement; the empirical evidence, theoretical analysis and supplementary limitations remain unchanged.
